textbookText: Project Work: Project 6.1 Measure the size of Earth’s Circumference by using the Eratosthenes technique. Hint: Materials you may require: Two poles(sticks)known as gnomons, measuring tape, protractor, and a synchronized time-keeping clock. Theory to execute: The difference in the angle made by the shadow with the pole in the two cases is equal to the angle subtended by the arc length between the poles at the centre. For ∆θ as the difference in the angle and X as the arc length, the circumference C is calculated as C/X = 360/∆θ⇒ C = 360 × 𝑋 ∆θ Procedural idea: i) Choose two distant locations on the Earth’s surface on the same meridian (line of longitude), ideally at north-south alignment. ii) Measure the distance X using a map or GPS. iii) Keep the poles at these locations and find the angle made by their shadows with the top of the respective poles exactly at the same time in the noon. It gives ∆θ . iv) Finally find the value of the circumference. Follow www. Google.com, U – tube Project 6.2 Execute the project work on “Study the value of g by using microgram weighing tool.”
